In addition to these programs there is the Indian Health Services Program (Public Law 83-568, 42 U.S.C. 2001-2004a.) which provides specialized health services to Indians. This program which includes planning assistance can effectively mitigate any impacts on health services for Indians in the coal resource area.
For small communities (less than 10,000 population) low interest loans, administered by the Farmers Home Administration, are available under the Rural Development Act of 1972, (P.L. 92-419) for community facilities which includes funds for hospitals, clinics, and nursing homes.
Additional School Facilities and Programs - will be a pressing need if a high level of coal development is achieved. These will require large amounts of capital investment and operational funds. Two educational assistance programs under HEW that apply to federally impacted areas may be available to the area impacted by Westmoreland Resources operations. P.L. 81-874 (as amended) is available for assisting in the operation and maintenance of schools and P.L. 81-815 (as amended) for construction of facilities. These are expected to apply, to at least some degree, in the impacted area. The eligibility of a school district and the level of assistance received depend on the number of children living on federal or trust property, the location of the jobs generated and the residence of the employee's family. These factors we all determine the extent to which these programs would mitigate educational programs.
